line_items.reasoning: JPM revised Markets NII downward from prior estimates predominantly due to lower rates, representing a net headwind to the ~$103B total NII guide, signaling the full-year NII target is now under pressure.

No explicit EPS guide was provided, but Q1 EPS of $5.94 and ROTCE of 23% are exceptionally strong outputs, with net income of $16.5B driven by broad-based revenue beats across CIB, AWM, and CCB — well above any implicit baseline.
Q1 expenses of $26.9B were up 14% YoY and outpaced revenue growth of 10%; annualizing Q1 implies ~$107.6B, which would exceed the ~$105B full-year expense guide if the elevated run rate persists.
Consumer credit metrics remain healthy with no signs of cracks — early roll rates, delinquency rates, and cash buffers are all consistent with prior trends, supporting the ~3.4% card NCO rate guide.

Average CCB deposits were up 2% YoY and QoQ, consistent with the 'modest firm-wide deposit growth' guidance; card loan growth trajectory was not explicitly flagged as deviating from the guided 6–7% range.
